quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, add extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a collision.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reactions and affects your decisions. You may fall asleep while driving, which can cause a crash and injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Speed up to protect your right-of-way.
Always stay in your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass other vehicles. It marks zones where passing is unsafe from that direction.

questions.question: After a collision, what should you do with injured people?

options.text: Move them far away from the road.
Do not move them unless absolutely necessary.
Tell them they are fine and don't need a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Moving injured people can make injuries worse. Only move them if there is fire or immediate danger. Have them sit or lie down and wait for medical help.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Have one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use the parking brake and put the vehicle in park.
Point your front wheels straight if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake and put the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake and put your vehicle in park. If there is no curb, turn your wheels away from the road center so the car rolls away safely if brakes fail. If there is a curb, point your wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: You should not start across an intersection if the light will turn red before you clear it. This applies:

options.text: In all cases.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all cases.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, how should you use it?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol in drivers under 21. Any trace of alcohol will result in strict penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water can hide dangers. If you see flooding, turn around and use a different route.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as you can.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: When are roads most slippery?

options.text: When it has rained hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after rain starts.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not yet washed away. Be extra careful in the first half hour of rain.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming cars.
Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance at night because it is harder to see. Use headlights correctly. Do not look at oncoming headlights, as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you remember?

options.text: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will drive at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even if you signal.

questions.question: This sign indicates:

options.text: The distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal height for vehicles in this state.
The maximum width allowed for vehicles on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It shows how far down the bridge or overpass is from the road surface (in this case, 12 feet, 6 inches).

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road will intersect ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road will intersect ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers to watch for a side road that is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beams. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together to protect you. Always wear your lap and shoulder belts, even if your vehicle has airbags.

questions.question: What can speed up the removal of alcohol from a person's body?

options.text: Nothing. Only time removes alcohol from your system.
Taking a cold shower.
Eating a large meal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing. Only time removes alcohol from your system.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane is ending. Drivers must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending. Drivers must merge left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign tells drivers that lanes are being reduced ahead and they need to merge left.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved ramp going downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before you enter the curve.
Slow down to the freeway's posted speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking while turning may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: You must always protect pedestrians. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what they are doing.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough space on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a town with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough space on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when you drive. An officer can ask for it anytime you are stopped or after a collision.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and hazards.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right and you also want to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus can turn.
Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices used in work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange warning signs on the road.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Always look left and right before entering an intersection, crosswalk, or railroad crossing. Make sure no one is coming from either side.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with no curb, turn your wheels right toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels left toward the center so your car rolls into the curb if the brakes fail.

questions.question: If you see animals standing near the roadway while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. Also, there may be more animals nearby that you cannot see yet.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then pull to the right and stop. You must always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as fines under normal conditions.
You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
Slow down only if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
questions.explanation: Always slow down in work zones. This protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: This sign indicates a:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn you about hazards ahead. Round signs are only used to warn about railroad crossings.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Nothing else—including eating and drinking—can speed up this process.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.
As your speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 mph, survival is very unlikely. Higher speeds also require longer stopping distances, so you need more following distance.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
Will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign means you are coming to a railroad crossing. You must look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May finish its turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space to turn. They often have to swing wide to complete a right turn safely.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. When the road is slippery, you should:

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
Test your tires' grip while driving uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce your tire grip. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. To avoid skidding, do not make quick turns or stops at high speeds.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, drive through quickly. If you have not entered, stop.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phones.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. Only move forward if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often causes unsafe decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often causes unsafe decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to drive through a red light at an intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Drive through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officers directing traffic override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows your nerves and body functions. It reduces your focus and ability to stay alert.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane. You should:

options.text: Enter the right lane and speed up to match traffic flow.
Use the road's shoulder to reach traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up to enter the interstate.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must drive safely. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.
